correctness.rationale: The support interval follows from Courant-Fischer interlacing and endpoint continuity. The cone-avoidance equivalence is proved by minimizing a positive quadratic form under one linear constraint; Haar disintegration produces the exact normalized CDF integral. Strict parameter monotonicity, the attained c=b bound and the unattained c-down-to-zero arcsine bound are analytic, not fitted. The upper-tail coefficient follows from dominated convergence and complete elliptic integrals, and is itself strictly identifying. The a=b point mass follows from 2-plane intersection dimension. A separate seeded 90,000-orientation orthogonal-compression checker verifies analytic event equivalences at five thresholds; it does not replace proof. No finite-sample rates are asserted.

value.rationale: The geometry of a three-dimensional ellipsoid observed only through unlabeled diameters of center-passing random planar sections is a motivated geometric stereology inverse problem. The natural sharp answer splits all ellipsoids into the identifiable strict-top-axis class and the nonidentifiable repeated-top-axis class; all triaxial cases require only two distribution-support extrema plus any single interior probability. The sharp prolate and flat-limit envelopes are nontrivial precise bounds, and the elliptic upper-tail coefficient offers a second exact recovery channel. These supply reusable benchmarks for information content of geometric sections; the result is not claimed to give finite-sample performance or a high-dimensional theorem.
